title: Why async code returns too early
subtitle: Understand promises before a race becomes a bug
learning_objective: Predict when asynchronous work completes and correctly await its result.

scenes.title: THE EMPTY RESULT
scenes.body: Your function fetches user data, but the caller sees undefined. The request still finishes later. What happened?

scenes.title: An async function returns a promise
scenes.body: Calling an async function gives you a Promise immediately. The value you want arrives when that promise settles—not when the function call first returns.

scenes.title: The fix
Common trap
scenes.body: Returning a promise is not the same as returning its resolved value. Await it, or return the promise and let the caller await it.

scenes.question: What does calling an async function return?
scenes.explanation: An async function always returns a Promise. A returned value becomes that promise's fulfillment value.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Trace the promise boundary. Await the result at the point where you actually need the value.
